recall.prompt: Name a polygon with 3–12 sides. Use its conventional name, not “n-gon”.
recall.explanation: Naming the less familiar side counts earns a higher authored tier.

recall.prompt: Name one of the triangle centers formed by medians, altitudes, or internal angle bisectors.
recall.explanation: Medians → centroid; altitudes → orthocenter; internal bisectors → incenter.

recall.prompt: Name a quadrilateral class in this lesson: one with 0, 1, or 2 parallel-side pairs, or a special parallelogram.
recall.scope: Use the source convention: trapezoid = exactly one parallel pair
recall.explanation: The course uses trapezium for no parallel sides; this convention varies by region.

recall.prompt: Name one coordinate-area or segment-location method taught in the module.
recall.scope: A method for area, midpoint, or division points
recall.explanation: These locate division points or calculate area from ordered coordinates.

recall.prompt: Name a line-equation form explicitly listed in this course.
recall.scope: A named form, rather than a specific equation
recall.explanation: Different forms encode different given information; vertical lines need special care.

recall.prompt: Name a conic section covered by the course.
recall.scope: One of the four conic types
recall.explanation: Circle is the e = 0 ellipse special case; parabola e = 1, ellipse 0 < e < 1, hyperbola e > 1.

recall.prompt: Name one essential part of a parabola: a point, line, or focal chord listed in the lesson.
recall.explanation: The vertex is halfway from focus to directrix along the axis; the focal chord is perpendicular to the axis.

recall.prompt: Name a defining part of an ellipse: center, axis, special axis endpoint, focus, directrix, or focal chord.
recall.scope: Use a geometric part, not a parameter letter
recall.explanation: Vertices end the major axis; covertices end the minor axis; directrices are perpendicular to the major axis.

recall.prompt: Name one hyperbola feature: a branch, axis, special point, asymptote, directrix, or focal chord.
recall.explanation: The conjugate-axis endpoints are reference points, not points on the curve.

recall.prompt: Name a prism part or section explicitly defined in the lesson.
recall.scope: Base, lateral feature, height, axis, vertex, or right section
recall.explanation: A right section is perpendicular to the lateral-edge direction. Altitude is perpendicular to the base planes.

recall.prompt: Name a solid in this family: a parallelepiped, its rectangular special case, or the all-equal-edge rectangular case.
recall.scope: Give one of the three solid names
recall.explanation: Every cube is a cuboid, and every cuboid is a parallelepiped; the reverse implications fail.

recall.prompt: Name a cylinder type featured in the course.
recall.scope: Circular, hollow, elliptic, right, or oblique
recall.explanation: Right/oblique describe inclination; circular/elliptic describe base shape; hollow describes a removed bore.

recall.prompt: Name a pyramid length explicitly distinguished in the lesson.
recall.scope: Height, slant height, edge, base apothem, or base circumradius
recall.explanation: Slant height, lateral edge, apothem, and circumradius refer to different segments.

recall.prompt: For the cone inscribed in a cube, name a dimension used to connect the two solids.
recall.scope: Cone radius, diameter, altitude, slant height, or cube edge
recall.explanation: For cube edge q: r = q/2, h = q, and slant height = q√5/2.

recall.prompt: Name a sphere-related object or surface explicitly covered: whole, half, shell, cap, segment, zone, or a circle section.
recall.scope: Give a geometric object, not an area formula
recall.explanation: A zone is curved surface; a segment is a solid. Wetted bowl area excludes the liquid’s exposed top.
